task: Fix the query timeout that started after the composite index was dropped during migration.

candidate_memories.content: 90% of product listing queries now exceed the 5-second timeout since migration M-42 dropped the composite index.
The composite index on (category_id, status, created_at DESC) must be recreated on the products table.
Migration M-42 dropped the index as part of a planned index rebuild that was never completed.
When a migration drops an index, include the recreate step in the same migration to prevent query degradation.
The composite index supports 3 of the 5 most frequent query patterns; recreating it will fix the timeout for all three.
The products table has 12 million rows; index creation will take approximately 8 minutes.
Session 6 note: the product search feature was launched with elastic search integration.
Old practice: indexes were created manually by the DBA team before migration tooling was adopted.
The database autovacuum is configured to run nightly for the products table.
A performance test in session 3 showed product listing at 200ms p99 with the old index.
Old migration guide: the index rebuild for M-42 was planned for the following sprint but was deprioritized.
After any index drop, monitor query plans before closing the migration to ensure performance is preserved.
Session 13 note: the search team added a new faceted filter for product attributes.
The read replica used for product listings is updated with a 100ms replication lag.
Session 8 note: the product image CDN was updated to use WebP format.
Category hierarchies are managed in a separate category service and joined at query time.
Index rebuilds on large tables should be done with CONCURRENTLY to avoid table locks.
The SEO team reported slow product page loads in session 15; they identified the query timeout.
Old query optimization note: a covering index was considered but rejected for the products table.
The product catalog is exported to the warehouse for analytics every hour.
